Oil mill.subject: Farm Machinery

Averruncator.subject: Farm Machinery
Averruncator.question: The _____ was Type of extended shears for pruning distant branches.
Averruncator.fact: An averruncator or pole pruner (American English) is a form of long shears used in arboriculture for averruncating or pruning off the higher branches of trees, etc.

Axe.subject: Farm Machinery
Axe.question: The _____ was Type of wedge tool.
Axe.fact: An axe (; sometimes spelled ax in American English; see spelling differences) is an implement that has been used for thousands of years to shape, split, and cut wood, to harvest timber, and as a weapon. The axe has many forms and specialised uses but generally consists of a head with a sharpened blade (also called a "bit") attached to a handle (also called "haft" or "helve").

Billhook.subject: Farm Machinery
Billhook.question: The _____ was Cutting tool.
Billhook.fact: A billhook or bill hook is a versatile cutting tool used widely in agriculture and forestry for cutting woody material such as shrubs, small trees and branches.

Broadfork.subject: Farm Machinery
Broadfork.question: The _____ was Gardening tool.
Broadfork.fact: The broadfork, also called a U-fork or grelinette, is a garden tool used to manually break up densely packed soil, including hardpan, to improve soil aeration and drainage. Broadforks are used as part of a no-till or reduced-till seedbed preparation process because they preserve the soil structure and avoid the resurfacing of weed seeds.

Brushcutter (garden tool).subject: Farm Machinery
Brushcutter (garden tool).question: The _____ was Powered garden tool.
Brushcutter (garden tool).fact: A brushcutter (also called a brush saw, clearing saw or gasoline goat) is a powered garden or agricultural tool used to trim weeds, small trees, and other foliage not accessible by a lawn mower or rotary mower. Various blades or trimmer heads can be attached to the machine for specific applications.

Chainsaw.subject: Farm Machinery
Chainsaw.question: The _____ was Portable handheld power saw with a rotating chain.
Chainsaw.fact: A chainsaw (or chain saw) is a portable handheld power saw that cuts with a set of teeth attached to a rotating chain driven along a guide bar. Modern chainsaws are typically gasoline or electric and are used in activities such as tree felling, limbing, bucking, pruning, cutting firebreaks in wildland fire suppression, harvesting of firewood, for use in chainsaw art and chainsaw mills, for cutting concrete, and cutting ice.

Dethatcher.subject: Farm Machinery
Dethatcher.question: The _____ was Device that removes thatch from lawns.
Dethatcher.fact: A dethatcher or lawn scarifier is a device that removes thatch from lawns. Types of dethatchers include motorized dethatchers or those that can be pulled behind a garden tractor.

Dibber.subject: Farm Machinery
Dibber.question: The _____ was Planting tool.
Dibber.fact: A dibber or dibble or dibbler is a pointed wooden stick for making holes in the ground so that seeds, seedlings or small bulbs can be planted. Dibbers come in a variety of designs including the straight dibber, T-handled dibber, trowel dibber, and L-shaped dibber.

Drawbar (haulage).subject: Farm Machinery
Drawbar (haulage).question: The _____ was Vehicle and trailer coupling.
Drawbar (haulage).fact: A drawbar is a solid coupling between a hauling vehicle and its hauled load. Drawbars are in common use with rail transport; road trailers, both large and small, industrial and recreational; and agricultural equipment.

Earth auger.subject: Farm Machinery
Earth auger.question: The _____ was Device for digging holes on the ground.
Earth auger.fact: An earth auger, earth drill, or post-hole auger is a drilling tool used for making holes in the ground. In the 19th century, the hand-operated earth auger became a common farm and construction tool in the US, and several inventors submitted patents for them.

Family farm.question: The _____ was Farm owned or operated by a family.
Family farm.fact: A family farm is generally understood to be a farm owned and/or operated by a family. Garden fork.fact: A garden fork, spading fork, or digging fork (in the past also an asparagus fork, the same name as a very different utensil) is a gardening implement, with a handle and a square-shouldered head featuring several (usually four) short, sturdy tines. Garden forks were originally made of wood, but the majority are now made of forged carbon steel or stainless steel.

Drag harrow.fact: A drag harrow, a type of spring-tooth harrow, is a largely outdated type of soil cultivation implement that is used to smooth the ground as well as loosen it after it has been plowed and packed.

Roller (agricultural tool).subject: Farm Machinery
Roller (agricultural tool).question: The _____ was Tool for flattening land or breaking up soil.
Roller (agricultural tool).fact: The roller is an agricultural tool used for flattening land or breaking up large clumps of soil, especially after ploughing or disc harrowing. Typically, rollers are pulled by tractors or, prior to mechanisation, a team of animals such as horses or oxen.

Seed.subject: Farm Machinery
Seed.question: The _____ was Reproductive structure in plants.
Seed.fact: In botany, a seed is a plant structure containing an embryo and stored nutrients in a protective coat called a testa. More generally, the term seed means anything that can be sown, which may include seed and husk or tuber.

Seedbed.subject: Farm Machinery
Seedbed.question: The _____ was Local soil where seeds are planted.
Seedbed.fact: A seedbed or seedling bed is the local soil environment in which seeds are planted.

Bulldozer.subject: Farm Machinery
Bulldozer.question: The _____ was Mobile machine which uses a frontal blade to push large volumes of material.
Bulldozer.fact: A bulldozer or dozer (also called a crawler or Track-type Tractor) is a large tractor equipped with a metal blade at the front for pushing material (soil, sand, snow, rubble, or rock) during construction work. Bulldozers are used heavily in large and small scale construction, road building, mining and quarrying, on farms, in heavy industry factories, and in military applications in both peace and wartime.

Hardpan.subject: Farm Machinery
Hardpan.question: The _____ was Dense layer of soil found below topsoil.

Mechanised agriculture.subject: Farm Machinery
Mechanised agriculture.question: The _____ was Agriculture using powered machinery.
Mechanised agriculture.fact: Mechanised agriculture or agricultural mechanisation is the use of machinery and equipment, ranging from simple and basic hand tools to more sophisticated, motorised equipment and machinery, to perform agricultural operations.

Motor fuel.subject: Farm Machinery
Motor fuel.question: The _____ was Drives the internal combustion engine.
Motor fuel.fact: A motor fuel is a fuel that is used to provide power to the engine (motor) of vehicles — typically a heat engine that produces thermal energy via oxidative combustion of liquid or gaseous fuel and then converts the heat into mechanical energy through reciprocating pistons or gas turbines.

Sales presentation.subject: Farm Machinery
Sales presentation.question: The _____ was Line of talk to persuade someone to buy something.
Sales presentation.fact: As a selling technique, a sales presentation or sales pitch is a line of talk that attempts to persuade someone or something, with a planned sales presentation strategy of a product or service designed to initiate and close a sale of the product or service.

Tow hitch.question: The _____ was Hard attachment point on a road vehicle, used to tow a trailer.
Tow hitch.fact: A tow hitch (or tow bar or trailer hitch in North America) is a device attached to the chassis of a vehicle for towing, or a towbar to an aircraft nose gear.

Vendor lock-in.subject: Farm Machinery
Vendor lock-in.question: The _____ was Switching costs inhibiting a change of vendor.
Vendor lock-in.fact: In economics, vendor lock-in, also called proprietary lock-in or customer lock‑in, makes a customer dependent on a vendor for products, unable to use another vendor without substantial switching costs. Vendor lock-in does the opposite: it makes it difficult to move from one solution to another.

Bran.subject: Farm Machinery
Bran.question: The _____ was Hard outer layers of cereal grain.
Bran.fact: Bran, also called miller's bran, is the component of a cereal grain consisting of the outer hard layers – the combined aleurone and pericarp – surrounding the endosperm. Corn (maize) bran also includes the pedicel (tip cap).

Colour sorter.subject: Farm Machinery
Colour sorter.question: The _____ was Machines that separate items by colours.
Colour sorter.fact: Color sorters or colour sorters (sometimes called optical sorters, digital sorters, or electronic color sorters) are machines used on production lines in bulk food processing and other industries.

Conveyor belt.subject: Farm Machinery
Conveyor belt.question: The _____ was Close-loop rubber band used in motorized conveying system.
Conveyor belt.fact: A conveyor belt is the carrying medium of a belt conveyor system (often shortened to a belt conveyor). A belt conveyor system consists of two or more pulleys (sometimes called drums), with a closed loop of carrying medium—the conveyor belt—that rotates about them.

Rice.subject: Farm Machinery
Rice.question: The _____ was Cereal grain and staple food.
Rice.fact: Rice is a cereal grain and, in its domesticated form, is the staple food of over half of the world's population, particularly in Africa and Asia. Rice is the seed of the grass species Oryza sativa (Asian rice)—or, less commonly, Oryza glaberrima (African rice).

Rice.subject: Farm Machinery
Rice.question: Rice has become commonplace in many cultures worldwide; in _____, 800 million tons were produced, placing it third after sugarcane and maize

Rice hull.subject: Farm Machinery
Rice hull.question: The _____ was Protective husk of rice grains.
Rice hull.fact: Rice hulls or husks are the hard protecting coverings of grains of rice. In addition to protecting rice during the growing season, rice hulls can be put to use as building material, fertilizer, insulation material, or fuel.

Rice huller.subject: Farm Machinery
Rice huller.question: The _____ was Machine for processing whole rice.
Rice huller.fact: A rice huller or rice husker is an agricultural machine used to automate the process of removing the chaff (the outer husks) of grains of rice.

Rice polisher.subject: Farm Machinery
Rice polisher.question: The _____ was Machine for polishing kernels of rice.
Rice polisher.fact: A rice polisher is a machine for buffing (or "polishing") kernels of rice to change their appearance, taste, and texture or for transforming brown rice into white rice.

Rice polisher.subject: Farm Machinery
Rice polisher.question: The first fully automated rice polishing machine is believed to have been patented by the English engineer and inventor Sampson Moore in _____

White rice.subject: Farm Machinery
White rice.question: The _____ was Milled rice that has had its husk, bran, and germ removed.
White rice.fact: In food processing, white rice is processed rice that has been through a rice milling process, where bran, husk, and germ are removed from whole-grains of brown rice. The development and spread of white rice over time resulted from historical changes in rice cultivation, trade, and advances in milling technology.
